data.name: Haayi
data.gender_notes: Haayi is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root 'hayy' meaning 'lively' or 'active'. This name signifies energy, vitality, and movement. The name Haayi carries the meaning “Lively, Active” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Haayi usually hope their child will grow to embody lively, active and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that embodies the spirit of life and activity, rooted in the Islamic belief of God's continuous creation.
data.etymology: Haayi belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lively, Active.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Haayi total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

historical_references.context: Haayi b. Akhtab was a Jewish chieftain of Khaybar oasis. He had taken refuge with the Muslim army during their siege of the oasis, but later betrayed the Muslims when he led a surprise attack against them. The Muslims, led by Caliph Umar ibn al-Khattab, marched on Khaybar and defeated Haayi. Umar granted Haayi a pardon and allowed him to remain in the oasis as long as he paid the jizya tax.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Kathir, Al-Bidayah wa-l-Nihayah, volume 4, page 212. The name Haayi carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Haayi b. Akhtab was a Jewish chieftain of Khaybar who had previously betrayed the Muslims during their siege of the oasis. Haayi's bravery and leadership earned him the respect of the Muslim community.
